confidence_notes: I ran six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for Kaohsiung prices. The price results were aggregated, crowdsourced cost-of-living indexes that mostly cite Numbeo-style data. Some of those pages were undated or older, such as a July 2023 snapshot. Beer, cappuccino and the inexpensive meal are reasonably supported. Draft beer was about US$1.6-2.05 for 0.5 L in those indexes, and I set the restaurant anchor slightly higher. Cappuccino was about US$2.5-2.9. An inexpensive meal was about US$3.6-5. The mid-range meal for two is less certain, because the sources ranged from about US$25 to about US$32 for two. Cocktail and wine are the weakest food and drink anchors. I found only scattered figures: one NT$200 cocktail data point from 2021, venue listings of about US$11-12 for top bars, and a Taipei chain listing wine at about NT$220 a glass. I set both from those figures and a rough premium over local beer, not from a solid Kaohsiung price list. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Taiwan and Kaohsiung. I did not search for or inspect any live booking pages or listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Kaohsiung is Taiwan's second-largest city and a port and business hub with moderate tourism. I treated it as cheaper than Taipei and similar to Taichung and Tainan on food and lodging.
